title: openapi-proxy definition
description: An openapi-proxy project: the OpenAPI documents it is made of, and the variants served from them.

version.description: The version of this format. Always 1.

project.description: The project's slug: the first part of every public URL, /v/<project>/<variant>. It is the project's identity; a deploy creates the project or updates the one with this slug.

name.description: What the project is called in the app. Left out, it is the slug.

instance.description: The address of the instance this is deployed to, for a self-hosted one. Left out, it is https://openapi-proxy.app.

visibility.description: Who may read this project's variants unless a variant says otherwise. Left out, it is the workspace's default.

overrides.description: Title, description and servers for every variant, instead of what the main document says. A variant can state its own.

title.description: The title readers see, instead of the document's.

description.description: The description readers see, instead of the document's.

servers.description: Where the API is reached, instead of the document's whole list. Tools use the first unless someone picks another.

items.description: One place the API is reached.

url.description: The address, starting with https://, http:// or /.

description.description: What this one is, such as "Production".

sources.description: The OpenAPI documents of the project, merged into one in this order. One source needs only url or file. With several, each has a name and exactly one says main: true.

items.description: One OpenAPI document: at a url, or in a file.

name.description: What this document is called. Required with several sources; it also names components that have to be renamed in a merge.

url.description: The address of the document. A deploy reads it where it runs and uploads what it finds.

file.description: The path of the document, relative to this file. A deploy uploads it.

main.description: With several sources: this is the one whose title, description and servers describe the merged document, and whose operations win where two define the same.

follow.description: For a url: the service keeps reading it, so the document stays current between deploys. Left out, it changes only with a deploy.

pathPrefix.description: Put in front of every path of this document, such as /billing.

variants.description: The documents served from the project, by slug: the second part of the public URL.

name.description: What the variant is called in the app. Left out, it is the slug.

icon.description: The icon it has in the app's navigation.

visibility.description: Who may read it: public (anyone with the URL) or private (an API key that reads it). Left out, it is the project's, then the workspace's default.

include.description: What is served. Left out, everything is, and so is what the API adds later. With it, only what it names is served.

tags.description: Tags. A tag is a rule: it also covers operations that get the tag later.

items.description: A tag, exactly as the document spells it.

operations.description: Operations, each by method and path as the document has them, such as "GET /v1/books".

items.description: An operation: its method in capitals, a space, and its path. A webhook is "POST webhook:<name>".

exclude.description: What is not served, whatever include says.

tags.description: Tags. A tag is a rule: it also covers operations that get the tag later.

items.description: A tag, exactly as the document spells it.

operations.description: Operations, each by method and path as the document has them, such as "GET /v1/books".

items.description: An operation: its method in capitals, a space, and its path. A webhook is "POST webhook:<name>".

overrides.description: Title, description and servers this variant states itself, key by key over the project's.

title.description: The title readers see, instead of the document's.

description.description: The description readers see, instead of the document's.

servers.description: Where the API is reached, instead of the document's whole list. Tools use the first unless someone picks another.

items.description: One place the API is reached.

url.description: The address, starting with https://, http:// or /.

description.description: What this one is, such as "Production".
